subject: Re: Clearing the runway — ClearBay capacity plan and renewal options
messages:
From: Heather Lim <heather.lim@clearbay.io>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@clearbay.io, ops@clearbay.io
Date: 2026-09-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity ahead of renewal — short notice surge

Markus,

Quick note from our ops team: we've seen a sustained increase in inference traffic the past 6 weeks tied to a new feature rollout. Historical averages are no longer predictive — our 95th percentile memory/throughput has jumped ~37% and we're bumping into queue backed-up windows during peak UTC mornings.

Our renewal for Dedicated (term ends Oct 31) is coming up. Before we sign a new commitment we need to understand options for:
- short-term burst capacity to cover peak mornings for the next 3–6 months
- resizing the committed base if the higher traffic persists
- an interim price tier for burst usage vs committed GPUs

Can we set a call this week? I attached a quick snapshot from our side (clearbay_utilization_2026Q3.csv) — hope that helps.

Thanks,
Heather Lim
Head of Platform Engineering
ClearBay

---
Attachments: clearbay_utilization_2026Q3.csv (csv, 42KB)

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Heather Lim <heather.lim@clearbay.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-09T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ahead of renewal — short notice surge

Hi Heather — thanks for the heads up and the CSV.

High level: this is exactly the kind of situation our "burst-bridge" pattern was designed for (short-lived surge + potential baseline growth). Before the call, can you confirm two quick items so we don't have to chase them live:
1) Expected window for the morning peaks (tz and local hour range)
2) SLO needs during the peak (p50/p95 latency expectations)

Initial idea from our side: keep your committed base near current effective throughput to preserve unit economics, add a temporary burst pool sized to cover observed 95th-percentile delta, and revisit after 3 months with utilization-based rebaseline. Pricing for the burst pool is different from committed GPUs; we can propose a blended rate for a 3–6 month bridge.

I’ve looped in Karthik to run a quick utilization projection and Vanessa to model billing mechanics and term options. Available for a 30m call tomorrow 11–11:30 PT if that works.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, Heather Lim <heather.lim@clearbay.io>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-11T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ahead of renewal — short notice surge

Heather / Markus — I pulled the CSV and ran a quick breakdown (summary below). Full spreadsheet is attached to this message in the console link.

Observations:
- Q3 (Jul–Sep) observed average committed utilization: 62%
- Recent 6-week tail: 95th-percentile token throughput is +38% vs Q2 baseline
- Peak window roughly 07:00–10:00 UTC (consistent 3-hour elevated tail)

Projection options (fast shortlist):
1) Conservative: keep current commit (80 A100-equivalent vCPUs), add 24 burst GPUs available on-demand for peaks. Expected p95 coverage ~88% of current peak, cost uplift ~14% qtrly.
2) Growth rebaseline: increase commit to 96 GPUs (20% uplift), include 12 burst GPUs for additional headroom. Expected long-term unit cost falls by ~6% vs purely burst. Requires 12-month term.
3) Short-term bridge (preferred for immediate risk): keep commit at 80, add 20 burst GPUs for 6 months with an "accelerated reconciliation" clause — after 3 months we run an auto-rebaseline and either convert portion of burst to committed (at a pre-agreed rate) or sunset burst.

Risk tradeoffs: converting bursts to commit improves unit pricing but locks ClearBay to higher monthly spend if traffic normalizes. Burst keeps flexibility but higher per-GPU token cost.

Attachments: proposed_burst_pricing_v2.pdf (pricing matrix), and a console link to detailed hourly charts: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/clearbay/utilization/2026Q3

My recommendation: Option 3 (Short-term bridge). It reduces immediate operational risk with limited term exposure and gives both teams measurable triggers for a rebaseline. If you want, we can prototype a canary of 8 GPUs for 2 weeks to validate the traffic shape before turning on the full burst pool.

-Karthik
Senior Capacity Planner
Redwood Inference

From: Heather Lim <heather.lim@clearbay.io>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@clearbay.io
Date: 2026-09-13T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ahead of renewal — short notice surge

Thanks Karthik — the analysis is helpful. A couple of clarifying asks from our side: 
- Can Redwood offer a 6-month bridge with an option to convert up to 50% of burst into committed at a fixed rate if we hit a utilization trigger? If so, what would the conversion rate look like?
- For procurement: we need a short addendum to the contract that covers burst pricing and a one-time invoice mechanism (we prefer a single monthly line item for committed + burst).

We like the canary idea. If you can stand up 8 GPUs for two weeks immediately, we’ll toggle the new feature beta for 10% of traffic and report back.

Heather Lim
Head of Platform Engineering
ClearBay

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Heather Lim <heather.lim@clearbay.io>, procurement@clearbay.io
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-15T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ahead of renewal — short notice surge

Heather — glad we're aligned. Proposed final approach below (call this the "burst-bridge" package):

Summary (what Redwood will deliver)
- Base commit: maintain 80 A100-equivalent GPUs at current T1 committed pricing for the next 12 months (term extension to Oct 31, 2027).
- Burst pool: 20 A100-equivalent GPUs available on-demand for 6 months. Burst billed monthly on a higher per-GPU rate.
- Conversion option: after 90 days, ClearBay may convert up to 10 burst GPUs to committed capacity at a pre-agreed conversion rate (converted GPUs count toward the 12-month term).
- Canary: provision 8 GPUs immediately for a 14-day canary; Redwood will monitor the same metrics and share daily short reports.
- Billing: single monthly invoice line item combining committed + burst with a breakout appendix.

Next steps
1) Vanessa will prepare the addendum (pricing + conversion language + invoicing appendix) and a clean DocuSign link by end of day Friday.
2) Karthik will provision the canary 8 GPUs within 24 hours of DocuSign signature and enable the burst pool gating controls.
3) After 90 days we'll run a utilization rebaseline and present recommended convert/retain/sunset options.

If that matches ClearBay's requirements I’ll route the addendum for signature. Happy to hop on one more quick call if you want to discuss conversion rates.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales — Dedicated
Redwood Inference
